## Dataset

* The Excel file `MANCAR_InBody_lab_10132026.xlsx` contains 231 rows from 31 distinct participant IDs (long format, one row per participant per visit). Variables include:
  * Participant data:
    * Status: `Finished` or `Dropped`
    * Treatment equence: Control-Mango or Mango-Control
    * Demographics: age and sex
    * Visit number (0-7) and date
    * Anthropometrics and body composition: height, weight, and InBody measurements
      * InBody measurements were taken at every visit
  * Biomarkers -- see the list of outcomes below
    * Units are defined in `MANCAR_InBody_lab_data dictionary_10142026.xlsx`
    * Biomarkers were measured at visits 0 (baseline), 3 (end of phase 1), and 7 (end of phase 2)

* Of the 31 participants:
  * 15 were randomized to the Control–Mango sequence and 
  * 16 were randomized to the Mango–Control sequence
  * One participant in the control–mango sequence and two in the mango–control sequence withdrew, leaving 14 completers in each sequence
    * MANCAR24, Control-Mango, Last seen at Visit 0 (baseline)
    * MANCAR17, Mango-Control, Last seen at Visit 1
    * MANCAR27, Mango-Control, Last seen at Visit 3 (completed phase 1 only)
    
```{r read_data}

# Read participant demog + biomarker data ---------------------------------

# Read data; n.obs = 231 from 31 distinct partIDs
# Remove variables that are not needed
bm_long <- read_excel("./data/MANCAR_InBody_lab_10132026.xlsx", na = c("", ".")) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(-matches("right|left|trunk|arm|leg|cellular|ecw|visceral|impedance|control|score|basal|smi")) %>% 
  rename(
    partid = part_id,
    seq    = gr_rand,
    height = x2_height,
    sex    = x3_gender,
    age    = x4_age,
    date   = x5_test_date_time,
    weight = x6_weight,
    tbw    = x7_tbw_total_body_water,
    dlm    = x10_dlm_dry_lean_mass,
    bfm    = x11_bfm_body_fat_mass,
    lbm    = x12_lbm_lean_body_mass,
    smm    = x13_smm_skeletal_muscle_mass,
    bmi    = x14_bmi_body_mass_index,
    pbf    = x15_pbf_percent_body_fat,
    tnfa   = tnf_alpha,
    il_1b  = il_1_beta,
    hdl    = hdl_cho_l,
    isop   = x8_isoprostanglin_f2a,
    oxldl  = oxidized_ldl
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    seq        = factor(seq, levels = c("C", "M"), labels = c("Control-Mango", "Mango-Control")),
    sex        = factor(sex),
    date       = as_date(dmy_hms(date)),
    phase      = case_when(
      visit == 0              ~ 0,
      visit >= 1 & visit <= 3 ~ 1,
      visit >= 4 & visit <= 7 ~ 2,
      ),
    phase      = factor(phase),
    trt        = case_when(
      phase == 0 ~ "Baseline",
      phase == 1 & seq == "Control-Mango" ~ "Control",
      phase == 2 & seq == "Control-Mango" ~ "Mango",
      phase == 1 & seq == "Mango-Control" ~ "Mango",
      phase == 2 & seq == "Mango-Control" ~ "Control",
    ),
    trt        = factor(trt),
    isop       = isop       / 1000,        # Convert to ng/mL
    crp        = crp        / 1000,        # Convert to mg/L
    e_selectin = e_selectin / 1000,        # Convert to ng/mL
    icam_1     = icam_1     / 1000,        # Convert to ng/mL
    vcam_1     = vcam_1     / 1000         # Convert to ng/mL
  ) %>% 
  select(partid, status, seq, visit, phase, trt, everything())

# Demographic variables
demog_vars <- c(
  "sex",
  "age",
  "bmi"
)

# Primary outcomes
primary_bm <- c(
  "glucose", 
  "insulin", 
  "homair", 
  "a1c", 
  "chol", 
  "ldl", 
  "hdl", 
  "trig", 
  "oxldl",
  "isop"
)

# Secondary outcomes
secondary_bm <- c(
  "crp", 
  "e_selectin", 
  "icam_1", 
  "vcam_1",
  "pbf", 
  "bfm",
  "lbm"
)

```

## Outcomes

* There are 17 outcomes (10 primary and 7 secondary)

* Primary outcomes:
  * Glycemic indicators:
    * Fasting glucose (mg/dL)
    * Fasting insulin (µIU/mL)
    * HOMA2-IR (from Oxford calculator)
    * HgbA1c (%)
  * Lipids
    * Total cholesterol (mg/dL)
    * LDL-cholesterol (mg/dL)
    * HDL-cholesterol (mg/dL)
    * Triglycerides (mg/dL)
  * Oxidative stress
    * Oxidized LDL-C (ng/mL)
    * 8-iso-PGF2α (ng/mL)^*^

* Secondary outcomes:
  * Inflammation markers:
    * C-reactive protein (mg/L)^*^
    * E-selectin (ng/mL)^*^
    * ICAM-1 (ng/mL)^*^
    * VCAM-1 (ng/mL)^*^
  * Body composition
    * Percent body fat (%)
    * Body fat mass (kg)
    * Lean body mass (kg)
    
^*^ Converted from the units in the raw data (pg/mL, or ng/mL for CRP) by dividing by 1,000.
    
## Exploratory analysis

### Anomalies

* The plot below shows visit number against visit date for each participant
  * Visits were approximately evenly spaced. The earliest visit was in October 2024 and the latest in February 2026
  * One participant (MANCAR28) has visit dates that are out of order relative to visit number:

```{r plot_visit_number_date, fig.height = 3, fig.width = 8}

# Visit date and visit number
bm_long %>%
  mutate(flag = partid == "MANCAR28") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = visit, group = partid)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = flag)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = flag), size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-01-07"), y = 0.4,
           label = "MANCAR28", hjust = 0.5, size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "red"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:7) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Visit number") +
  theme_bw()
```

* Visit dates for MANCAR28 are out of order:
  * Visits 0 and 1 are dated Jan–Feb 2026, while visits 2–7 run from Jul to Dec 2025.
  * The dates appear correct, but the visit numbers seem to be shifted by two?
    * i.e., labeled visits 2–7 are actually visits 0–5, and labeled visits 0–1 are actually visits 6–7?
  * To be confirmed with the study team

```{r visit_date_anomalies}

```

### Distribution

* Histograms of all outcomes, pooled across visits 0, 3, and 7, are shown below:
  * Some of the outcomes are right-skewed and need to be log-transformed
  * The largest outlier in insulin was observed in MANCAR21 at visit 3 (insulin 119 µIU/mL, glucose 147 mg/dL). HOMA2-IR was not calculated with this insulin value (above the Oxford calculator’s upper limit)

### Profile plots

* See the [interactive profile plots](https://keijioda.github.io/mango_cardio/profile_plots.html)
  for all outcomes (hover over a line to see a participant's values).

#### Profile plots for glycemic indicators:
* MANCAR24 (Control–Mango) had high glucose (139 mg/dL), HOMA2-IR (3.75), and HbA1c (6.8%)
  at baseline, and then dropped out.
* MANCAR27 (Mango–Control) had high glucose at baseline (154 mg/dL) and at visit 3 (158 mg/dL),
  and then dropped out.
* [**Check needed**] MANCAR21 (Mango–Control) had a spike in glucose (147 mg/dL) and insulin (119 µIU/mL) at visit 3,
  suggesting a non-fasting sample; HOMA2-IR was not calculated for this visit (insulin above the Oxford calculator's upper limit)
* [**Check needed**] MANCAR22 (Mango–Control) had the largest drop in glucose from Mango to Control (139 → 94 mg/dL).
  Insulin was consistently high at all visits (38.4–50.7 µIU/mL).
* [**Check needed**] MANCAR16 (Control–Mango) showed a steep decline in insulin (10.1 → 2.5 → 2.0 µIU/mL);
  HOMA2-IR is missing at visits 3 and 7 because insulin was below the Oxford calculator's lower limit.

```{r profile_plot_glycemic, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}

# Profile plots
# Outcome labels
outcome_labels <- c(
  glucose    = "Glucose (mg/dL)",
  insulin    = "Insulin (µIU/mL)",
  homair     = "HOMA2-IR",
  a1c        = "HbA1c (%)",
  chol       = "Total chol (mg/dL)",
  ldl        = "LDL-C (mg/dL)",
  hdl        = "HDL-C (mg/dL)",
  trig       = "TG (mg/dL)",
  oxldl      = "Ox-LDL (ng/mL)",
  isop       = "8-iso-PGF2α (ng/mL)",
  crp        = "CRP (mg/L)",
  e_selectin = "E-selectin (ng/mL)",
  icam_1     = "ICAM-1 (ng/mL)",
  vcam_1     = "VCAM-1 (ng/mL)",
  pbf        = "Body fat (%)",
  bfm        = "Fat mass (kg)",
  lbm        = "Lean mass (kg)"
)

# Function for profile plot
plot_profile <- function(data, var, ylab = outcome_labels[[var]], log = FALSE) {
  p <- data %>%
    filter(visit %in% c(0, 3, 7), !is.na(.data[[var]])) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = visit, y = .data[[var]], group = partid, color = seq)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~ seq) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 3, 7), minor_breaks = 0:7) +
    labs(x = "Visit", y = if (log) paste(ylab, "(log scale)") else ylab, title = outcome_labels[[var]]) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  if (log) p <- p + scale_y_log10() + guides(y = guide_axis_logticks())
  p
}

# Profile plots for glycemic indicators
(plot_profile(bm_long, "glucose") + plot_profile(bm_long, "insulin", log = TRUE)) /
(plot_profile(bm_long, "homair", log = TRUE) + plot_profile(bm_long, "a1c"))

```

#### Profile plots for lipids:
* Lipid levels were generally stable within participants, particularly HDL-C;
  no consistent pattern by treatment phase is apparent
* MANCAR10 (Control–Mango) had the highest total cholesterol (272–283 mg/dL) and LDL-C
  (168–185 mg/dL) throughout, and the highest triglycerides at baseline (314 mg/dL).
* [**Check needed**] MANCAR31 (Mango–Control) showed a large drop in total cholesterol (231 → 187 mg/dL)
  and LDL-C (172 → 121 mg/dL) from visit 3 to visit 7 (control phase)
* [**Check needed**] MANCAR22 (Mango–Control) had a rise in total cholesterol (287 mg/dL), LDL-C (190 mg/dL),
  and triglycerides (235 mg/dL) at visit 7 (control phase).
* Three participants in the Mango–Control sequence had a dip in LDL-C at visit 3
  (end of mango phase): MANCAR25 (115 → 81 → 118 mg/dL), MANCAR32 (113 → 79 → 108 mg/dL),
  and MANCAR23 (97 → 78 → 78 mg/dL).
* MANCAR02 (Mango–Control) had consistently high HDL-C (76–85 mg/dL).
* Dropouts: MANCAR24 (Control–Mango) had baseline values only (total cholesterol 249 mg/dL,
  LDL-C 159 mg/dL); MANCAR27 (Mango–Control) had high HDL-C (78 and 75 mg/dL) at baseline
  and visit 3.

```{r profile_plot_lipids, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}

# Profile plots for lipids
(plot_profile(bm_long, "chol") + plot_profile(bm_long, "ldl")) /
(plot_profile(bm_long, "hdl") + plot_profile(bm_long, "trig"))

```

#### Profile plots for oxidative markers:

* Oxidized LDL showed a pattern consistent with a mango effect: values decreased during
  the mango phase and increased during the control phase in both sequences
* Oxidized LDL levels were generally higher in the Control–Mango sequence
* MANCAR31 (Mango–Control) had a marked decrease during the control phase (384 → 224 ng/mL),
  in parallel with the drop in LDL-C noted above.
* 8-iso-PGF2α showed no consistent pattern by treatment phase. MANCAR35 (Control–Mango) had
  consistently low values (0.26–0.37 ng/mL).

```{r profile_plot_oxidation, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3}

# Profile plots for oxidation
plot_profile(bm_long, "oxldl") + plot_profile(bm_long, "isop", log = TRUE)

```

#### Profile plots for inflammatory markers:

* [**Check needed**] CRP: MANCAR26 (Control–Mango) had a spike at visit 7 (0.80 → 9.12 mg/L), suggesting an acute inflammatory episode.
* E-selectin: MANCAR24 (Control–Mango) had a high value at baseline (75.9 ng/mL), then dropped out.
* ICAM-1: MANCAR02 (Mango–Control) had consistently high values (1,211–1,298 ng/mL) and
  MANCAR05 (Control–Mango) consistently low values (~28 ng/mL); MANCAR31 (Mango–Control)
  increased from 484 to 885 ng/mL at visit 3.
* [**Check needed**] VCAM-1: MANCAR16 (Control–Mango) increased steadily (795 → 865 → 1,080 ng/mL);
    MANCAR25 (Mango–Control) had a spike at visit 3 (1,140 ng/mL); MANCAR33 (Mango–Control)
    had consistently low values (189–243 ng/mL).

```{r profile_plot_inflammation, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}

# Profile plots for inflammation
(plot_profile(bm_long, "crp", log = TRUE) + plot_profile(bm_long, "e_selectin")) /
(plot_profile(bm_long, "icam_1") + plot_profile(bm_long, "vcam_1"))

```

#### Profile plots for body composition:

* Body fat:
  * MANCAR27 (Mango–Control) increased during the mango phase (35.2% → 38.5%) before dropping out.
* Fat mass:
  * MANCAR22 (Mango–Control) decreased during the control phase (48.3 → 44.3 kg).
  * MANCAR27 (Mango–Control) increased during the mango phase (23.5 → 27.5 kg) before dropping out.
* Lean mass: Very stable within participants

```{r profile_plot_body_composition, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}

# Profile plots for body composition
(plot_profile(bm_long, "pbf") + plot_profile(bm_long, "bfm"))/
(plot_profile(bm_long, "lbm") + plot_spacer())

```

### Waterfall plots

* Each bar shows the within-participant difference between the end of the mango phase and the
  end of the control phase (mango − control) for completers. For skewed outcomes (insulin,
  HOMA2-IR, triglycerides, 8-iso-PGF2α, and CRP), the log ratio, log(mango / control), is shown.
  Bars are colored by treatment sequence.
  
```{r Waterfall_primary, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7.2}
# Waterfall plot
log_vars <- c("insulin", "homair", "trig", "isop", "crp")   # same as the log-scale models

plot_dat <- bm_long %>%
  filter(visit %in% c(3, 7)) %>%
  select(partid, seq, trt, all_of(c(primary_bm, secondary_bm))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(partid, seq, trt), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(partid, seq, outcome), names_from = trt, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = if_else(outcome %in% log_vars, log(Mango / Control), Mango - Control),
         partid  = parse_number(partid),
         outcome = factor(outcome, levels = names(outcome_labels))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff)) %>%
  mutate(bar = fct_reorder(paste(outcome, partid), diff))

wf_labels <- outcome_labels
wf_labels[log_vars] <- paste0(outcome_labels[log_vars], "\nlog ratio")

plot_waterfall <- function(vars, ncol = 4) {
  plot_dat %>%
    filter(outcome %in% vars) %>%
    droplevels() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = bar, y = diff, fill = seq)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free", ncol = ncol,
               labeller = as_labeller(wf_labels)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) sub(".* ", "", x)) +
    labs(x = "Participant ID", y = "Mango − Control (difference or log ratio)", fill = "Sequence") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
}

# Waterfall plots for primary outcomes
plot_waterfall(primary_bm, ncol = 4)

```
 
* Glycemic indicators:
  * Glucose, insulin, HOMA2-IR, and HbA1c showed no consistent direction; participants were
    split roughly evenly between lower and higher values on mango (e.g., glucose 14 vs 14).
  * The largest positive glucose differences came from MANCAR22 (139 vs 94 mg/dL), whose glucose dropped 
    during the control phase, and MANCAR21 (147 vs 107 mg/dL), whose end-of-mango sample was likely 
    non-fasting (see "Profile plots for glycemic indicators" section above). 
    The largest insulin difference was also from MANCAR21.
  * HbA1c differences were small and discrete (0.1% steps); 6 of 28 had no change.
  
* Lipids:
  * Total cholesterol was evenly split (14 vs 14). LDL-C tended to be slightly lower on mango
    (15 lower, 11 higher); the largest positive difference (+51 mg/dL) was from MANCAR31, whose LDL-C dropped 
    during the control phase (see "Profile plots for lipids" section above).
  * HDL-C tended to be slightly lower on mango (17 lower, 8 higher).
  * Triglycerides tended to be higher on mango in 18 of 28 participants.
  
* Oxidative stress:
  * Oxidized LDL was lower on mango in 20 of 28 participants.
  * 8-iso-PGF2α showed no consistent direction.

```{r Waterfall_secondary, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.8}

# Waterfall plots for secondary outcomes
plot_waterfall(secondary_bm, ncol = 4)

```

* Inflammatory markers:
  * CRP was lower on mango in 21 of 28 participants; the largest positive difference was MANCAR26, with a spike at the end of the mango phase (see "Profile plots for inflammatory" section above).

* Body composition:
  * Body fat (%) and fat mass were evenly split overall, but bars were largely separated by sequence: 
      * Control–Mango participants (mango in phase 2) mostly had positive differences and Mango–Control participants 
        (mango in phase 1) mostly negative, consistent with an increase in phase 2 regardless of diet (period effect).
  * Lean mass tended to be higher on mango (17 of 28).
